key_insight: A thermodynamically constrained neural network can learn phase-change rates between vapour, liquid, and ice and embed them into a discontinuous Galerkin atmospheric model while conserving mass and energy.
engineering_relevance: This provides a surrogate microphysics option for sub-kilometre convection simulations that could reduce reliance on expensive physics-based moist-process parameterisations.
method: Trained on convection-resolving output from a regional LFRic model using the CASIM microphysics scheme.
Network predicts mass exchanges among vapour, liquid, and ice under thermal/mechanical equilibrium assumptions.
Entropy change is derived from the learned exchanges to enforce energy consistency in the DG moist atmosphere model.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated by running a 2D vertical-slice non-hydrostatic DG atmosphere simulation and comparing three-phase cloud formation against a physics-based equilibrium moist-process representation.
watch_item: Because the surrogate is trained on a specific regional configuration and equilibrium assumptions, its robustness outside the training regime and in strongly non-equilibrium conditions may be limited.
paper_title: Data driven non-equilibrium moist phase exchanges for atmospheric convection within a discontinuous Galerkin model of the compressible Euler equations
